record.paper_title: Higher Rank Brill-Noether Theory and Coherent Systems: Open Questions
record.original_question: What is a mathematically satisfactory definition of alpha-stability for twisted coherent systems, one that behaves well geometrically and supports the construction of moduli spaces?

evidence.quote: Question 2.10. What is a “good” definition of α-stability for twisted coherent systems?

artifact.status_search_result: A literature search shows continuing work on $\alpha$-stability of (ordinary) coherent systems on curves and surfaces, including recent papers from 2024–2025 on $\alpha$-stability and linear stability of generated coherent systems and on stability conditions for coherent systems on integral curves. No source identifies a generally accepted "good" definition of $\alpha$-stability for the twisted version, suggesting the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: On α-stability and linear stability of generated coherent systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies α-stability for coherent systems on curves; works in the classical (untwisted) setting.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on α-stability for ordinary coherent systems, with no settled twisted analogue.

status_evidence.title: Stability conditions for coherent systems on Integral Curves
status_evidence.snippet: Recent investigation of stability conditions for coherent systems.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of the right stability notion for coherent systems remains under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Some moduli spaces of α-stable coherent systems on algebraic surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs moduli of α-stable coherent systems on surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations of α-stability are still being formulated; no twisted-curve definition is established.
